Il n’y a en tout cas pas de tons absolus. Les adjectifs et participes épithètes ainsi que les génitifs sont proclitiques. new_statements.quote: Les syllabes non accentuées sont prononcées nettement, sans altération des voyelles. L'accent est mélodique, montant ou descendant, et mériterait plus de recherches. Il n'y a en tout cas pas de tons absolus. Les adjectifs et participes épithètes ainsi que les génitifs sont proclitiques. Les noms sont accentués sur la syllabe finale ; quelques suffixes nominaux sont accentués, ainsi les marques de pluriel -mi/-bi et -ar. Comme les formes verbales indépendantes, les adverbes de lieu ont un accent initial, avec un allongement expressif de la première syllabe. La place de l'accent permet de repérer la catégorie du mot, et distingue des formes segmentalement identiques.
new_statements.translation: Unaccented syllables are pronounced clearly, without vowel alteration. The accent is melodic, rising or falling, and would merit more research. In any case there are no absolute tones. Attributive adjectives and participles as well as genitives are proclitic. Nouns are accented on the final syllable; some nominal suffixes are accented, e.g. the plural markers -mi/-bi and -ar. Like independent verb forms, adverbs of place have initial accent, with expressive lengthening of the first syllable. The place of the accent makes it possible to identify the word's category and distinguishes segmentally identical forms.
new_statements.citation: Authier, Gilles. 2009. Grammaire kryz (langue caucasique d'Azerbaïdjan, dialecte d'Alik). Collection Linguistique SLP 93. Leuven/Paris: Peeters. §2.8.2 'Accent de mot et parties du discours', p. 26.
new_statements.locator: printed p. 26, §2.8.2 (PDF page 30 of the uncorrected proofs); restated pp. 141 (§10.1), 143 (§10.1.4), 185 (§13.1)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (435 pp., text layer; source URL http://www.digitorient.com/wp/wp-content/uploads/2009/12/AUTHIERKryzGrammarUncorrectedproofs.pdf re-checked live today: HTTP 200, Content-Length 2287226 = copies we hold size). PDF page 30 = printed p. 26 carries the header "26 GRAMMAIRE KRYZ" and section "2.8.2. Accent de mot et parties du discours"; the quoted passage is there word for word (extracted text only differs by line-break hyphens: "procli-tiques"). The paragraph continues exactly as the reader summarised: nominalised dependent verb forms (masdars, gerunds/converbs, substantivised participles) have final accent, independent verb forms initial accent, minimal pairs yi-qr-íc 'saisir' / yí-qr…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word-class-conditioned pitch accent: nouns and all nominalised/dependent verb forms (masdars, gerunds, converbs, substantivised participles, also the future built on the imperfective participle and the interrogative forms) carry the accent on the final syllable; independent finite verb forms (all indicative forms except the future) and place adverbs carry it on the initial syllable. Accent position distinguishes segmentally identical forms: yi-qr-íc 'to seize' (masdar) vs yí-qr-ic 'was seized' (aorist N); xhiyíc 'to become' vs xhíyic 'became'; b-ar-í 'done / who did them' vs b-ár-i 'let them be done'. The author describes the accent as melodic (pitch), rising or falling, and explicitly denies lexical tone.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not described as such; the negative future (a compound form) 'keeps two accents', that of the imperfective participle and of the independent negative copula (p. 150).
new_statements.exceptions: Future tense keeps the participle's final accent (p. 143); interrogative verb forms are final-accented (p. 144); nominal plural suffixes -mi/-bi and -ar attract the accent; adjectives, attributive participles and genitives are proclitic (unaccented); adjective loses its accent when attributive (p. ~350: 'tonique, et perd son accent s'il est épithète'); forms without final accent drop the pharyngeal of the locative -aˤ (p. 31). Borise 2018 (citing Saadiev 1994: 411) instead reports second-syllable stress on di- and trisyllabic nominals, which agrees with Authier only for disyllables.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level accent in the Alik dialect (Authier's data); at phrase level each constituent carries one pitch accent, on the last syllable of the nominal head base and the first syllable of the verb (p. 185). Author notes the accent is melodic and under-researched; no instrumental study.
new_statements.identity_note: Authier 2009 describes the Alik dialect (village of Alik/Əlik, Quba district; Khaput is very close to it) and states the finite verb forms differ considerably across the three dialects Kryz, Djek, Alik-Khaput; Glottolog lists no separate dialect glottocodes under kryt1240. Saadiev's sketches describe the Kryz-village dialect (and a now-extinct Ismayilli variety). Borise 2018's 'second syllable' for nominals (from Saadiev 1994: 411) vs Authier's 'final syllable' may reflect this dialect difference or a description difference; unresolved without Saadiev.

sources.note: p.10 (§5.2): 'stress placement varies by part of speech in Kryz. In Kryz, di- and trisyllabic nominals, including deverbal nominals such as masdars, are stressed on the second syllable, while most verbs (apart from future forms) and adverbs have initial stress. This leads to minimal pairs: jiqhríd͡ʒ 'grab.INF', jíqhrid͡ʒ 'grab.PST.PTCP' (Saadiev 1994: 411; Authier 2009: 26, 141).' Secondary; note 'second syllable' (attributed to Saadiev) vs Authier's 'final syllable' for nouns.
